options: Creates all resources defined in the configuration
Downloads required providers and prepares the working directory, without touching real infrastructure
Deletes the current state and starts over
Shows a diff of pending changes
questions.explain: init downloads the providers declared in required_providers and sets up the local working directory. It does not create, modify, or destroy any real infrastructure.

questions.q: In `terraform plan` output, what does a `+` next to a resource mean?
options: The resource will be destroyed
The resource will be created
The resource is unchanged
The resource has an error
questions.explain: A plus sign in plan output marks a resource that will be created. A tilde (~) means update in place, and a minus (-) means destroy.

questions.q: What is the key difference between `terraform plan` and `terraform apply`?
options: plan changes infrastructure; apply only previews it
plan only shows what would change; apply shows the same plan, asks for confirmation, and then actually makes the changes
They are identical commands with different names
apply can only be run once per configuration ever
questions.explain: plan shows a preview with no changes made. apply performs the same comparison, displays the plan, and after confirmation (typing "yes"), actually creates, updates, or destroys resources.

questions.q: In what order does `terraform destroy` tear down the resource group and storage account from this lesson's example?
options: Resource group first, then storage account
Storage account first, then resource group — reverse of the creation order
Both are destroyed simultaneously with no order
Whichever one was declared first in the file
questions.explain: destroy tears resources down in reverse dependency order: the storage account (which depends on the resource group) is destroyed first, then the resource group itself.

questions.q: Why might `terraform apply` be run with `-auto-approve` in a CI/CD pipeline?
options: To skip generating a plan entirely
To skip the interactive yes/no prompt, appropriate once a human has already reviewed the plan elsewhere in the pipeline
Because CI/CD pipelines cannot run terraform plan
Because auto-approve disables the dependency graph
questions.explain: -auto-approve skips the interactive confirmation prompt, which makes sense in automated pipelines where the plan has already been reviewed as a separate step.
